name: Pyoderma Gangrenosum

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Delphi Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Pyoderma Gangrenosum

criteria.description: Rapid progression of a painful, necrolytic cutaneous ulcer with an irregular, undermined violaceous border
Exclusion of infectious causes of cutaneous ulceration
History of pathergy or development of new lesions at sites of trauma
Presence of associated systemic diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease, arthritis, or hematologic malignancy
Histopathologic findings consistent with neutrophilic dermatosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Both major criteria plus at least two minor or supportive criteria
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and by exclusion; biopsy is supportive but not definitive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rapidly progressive painful cutaneous ulcer with undermined violaceous borders
searchTerms: deep painful skin wound with raised borders

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pathergy phenomenon (lesion development at sites of minor trauma)

common.symptomName: Associated systemic symptoms such as fever and malaise
searchTerms: systemic symptoms like malaise and fever

occasional.symptomName: Inflammatory bowel disease symptoms (diarrhea, abdominal pain)
searchTerms: bowel disease signs like stomach cramps
lung inflammation with white blood cells

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to systemic disease
searchTerms: brain or nerve problems due to disease
neurological signs caused by systemic condition

laboratory: Negative bacterial cultures from ulcer base
imaging: Chest imaging if pulmonary involvement suspected
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; association with autoinflammatory syndromes reported
other: Histopathology showing neutrophilic dermatosis with sterile dermal infiltrate
Exclusion of infectious, neoplastic, and vascular causes

distinguishingFeatures: Rapidly spreading infection with systemic toxicity
Presence of ANCA or other autoantibodies
Lack of rapid progression typical of PG

redFlags: Rapid ulcer enlargement with systemic toxicity
Failure to respond to immunosuppressive therapy
Signs of secondary infection or sepsis
references: Brooklyn TN, Dunnill MG, Probert CS. Diagnosis and treatment of pyoderma gangrenosum. BMJ. 2006;333(7560):181-184.
Marzano AV, et al. Pyoderma gangrenosum: a clinical review. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol. 2017;31(5): 767-777.
Delphi Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Pyoderma Gangrenosum. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2018;79(4): 608-615.
